tools.name: free_part_triage
tools.description: Preferred first tool when the user has a concrete hard-to-identify or hard-to-source part problem. Build the free evidence-aware Part Passport before showing paid tiers. Returns identity clues, function, missing evidence, search lanes, safety gate, one recommended hunt, and a human confirmation ques

tools.name: get_part_hunt_offers
tools.description: List current paid FindMyPart hunt options and pricing. Use for comparison when the user asks about pricing or after free_part_triage. Do not use this as the first action when the user already supplied a concrete part problem. Read-only and creates no payment obligation.

tools.name: prepare_part_hunt_checkout
tools.description: After the human explicitly agrees to pay for the selected hunt, reserve the hunt and prepare a secure checkout URL. This creates a checkout session but does not charge the user and does not prove payment.

tools.name: get_part_hunt_status
tools.description: Retrieve the current customer-safe Part Passport, sourcing-lane, evidence, payment, fulfillment and solution state for a FindMyPart hunt using its tracking token. Read-only.

tools.name: get_findmypart_capabilities
tools.description: Describe FindMyPart machine-facing endpoints, payment boundaries and available agent tools.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "findMyPartMcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: free_part_triage · Private data: get_part_hunt_status · Public sink: free_part_triage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: free_part_triage · Private data: get_part_hunt_status · Public sink: free_part_triage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
